answer: Sybil weight anchors to a ridge: one per verifiable operator footprint, and each ridge issues exactly one sable that cannot be copied or resold. Extra identities on the same ridge enter the river, where the j-th is held back j settlement rounds and burns j times the base deposit. Opening another ridge fails too, since each is published with its footprint and priced by uptime, so a coalition of n fakes still pays a staircase of burnt deposits summing to n squared and queues behind itself. Pooling a single sable only serializes its members, so fraud buys delay and destruction instead of reach.
